newsitem.title: USA: U.S. judge schedules Friday hearing on UPS motion.
newsitem.headline: U.S. judge schedules Friday hearing on UPS motion.

text.p: A federal judge in Boston scheduled a hearing for Friday on a motion by United Parcel Service of America Inc to prevent strikers from interfering with the giant shipper's operations.

U.S. District Judge George O'Toole scheduled an 1100 EDT (1500 GMT) hearing in Boston federal court, his clerk said. The motion seeks to prevent striking Teamsters in Massachusetts from interfering with the company's operations.
At least 47 strikers have been arrested in clashes with police at UPS facilities in the Boston area since the job action began at midnight Sunday, according to the motion.
Similar motions were also filed in a court in Ontario, Calif., and other areas where workers have tried to block business operations, UPS spokeswoman Jennifer Jiles confirmed.
Jiles said workers have tried to block working employees from entering facilities and delivery trucks from leaving at plants in Boston and Ontario, Calif., and elsewhere.

"There are other areas dispersed sporadically around the country where there have been incidents," she said. "They have been doing things like lying down on the road. For their own safety, we are doing this," she added. Meanwhile, talks between the striking Teamsters and UPS resumed in Washington.
